thread.title: Apple’s event will be about more than just the iPhone

author: Emily Bary
title: Apple’s event will be about more than just the iPhone
text:
The iPhone always steals the show at Apple Inc.’s annual September event, but it won’t be the only device that gets some love from the world’s most valuable company at its biggest launch event.
Apple AAPL, +2.53% has typically made a variety of hardware announcements at its iPhone launch events, and it’s likely to debut a new version of the Apple Watch at this year’s confab, scheduled for Wednesday at the company’s new Cupertino, Calif., headquarters. The company could also announce upgrades to other products, including the AirPods, and share more information about its streaming-media progress.
Don’t miss: What to expect for the iPhone the Apple event
The iPhone continues to bring in the bulk of Apple’s revenue—56% of total revenue in the fiscal third quarter—but other products will become increasingly important for the company as it builds out its ecosystem. The company often points to wearables during its earnings calls as an example of a category showing fast expansion and helping to maintain brand loyalty. Watch and iPad revenues are projected to be up on the year.
Reports indicate that Apple is preparing to launch the Apple Watch Series 4, which is expected to feature a bezel-free design that will allow for more usable screen space in a similarly sized frame. According to 9to5Mac, which shared a photo of the expected watch , the Series 4 will offer roughly 15% more screen real estate.
The invitations Apple sent out for the event featured a “Gather Round” tag line , leading some to joke that the company might be about to debut a round smartwatch. IDC research director Ramon Llamas told MarketWatch that he thinks that’s “absolutely not” going to happen, though he wishes the company would create a device “that looks like a watch and not a shrunken down display.”
See also: Apple officially becomes first U.S. company with $1 trillion market cap
Feature-wise, Llamas said it’s possible that Apple looks for ways to make its cellular-enabled version more appealing, perhaps by introducing navigation and more location-based services via an LTE connection. He’s also hoping for enhanced battery life with the newest version.
The company announced in June that its new watch operating system will allow for easier access to Siri, better activity tracking and fitness competitions.
Apple may be feeling pressure to add compelling features to its new watch following a recent report indicating that consumers in the second quarter overwhelmingly chose the cheaper, older Series 1 model over the Series 3 version, which is Apple’s latest. Analysts at Counterpoint Research found that many who wanted a non-cellular Apple Watch didn’t see enough reason to justify the GPS-only Series 3’s higher price point and thus went with the Series 1.
While analysts seem generally confident that Apple will update the Watch at its event, there’s some debate about what other products will be featured. Some say the company’s popular AirPod earbuds could also be in for a refresh this year.
“As markets for truly wireless earphones gets crowded, we could see AirPods 2 with water resistance and wireless charging cases,” wrote RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani, who rates the stock at outperform with a $240 price target.

Apple gave a preview of its AirPower wireless charging mat a year ago and it’s been all silence since. Daryanani said that the company could finally launch this device this year “in a further push to accessories.”
Morgan Stanley’s Katy Huberty said that a charging mat remains an “unknown at this point,” but that the timing seems to make sense given that Apple first talked about the product a year ago.
Huberty does expect the company to offer an 11-inch edge-to-edge iPad featuring FaceID as well as provide “an update to the Mac portfolio.” She rates the stock at overweight with a $245 target price.
Read: Apple says proposed tariffs would hit the Apple Watch, AirPods, Mac Mini, and other products
Goldman Sachs analyst Rod Hall wrote that he “wouldn’t be surprised to see” a low-end MacBook Pro laptop that’s priced closer to the MacBook Air, as well as a “refresh of the Mac Mini.” He calls the potential for other product announcements “interesting but not very material.”
Hall has a neutral rating and $240 target price on the stock.

Not all are convinced that the Mac will get attention this month. Bernstein’s Toni Sacconaghi, who has a market-perform rating and $200 price target on Apple shares, wrote that he believes a new MacBook Air with retina display will be the focus of a future announcement, possibly to take place in October.
Though Apple’s fall event tends to focus on hardware, the company could share more about various software- and service-oriented themes this week. In particular, many analysts want to hear about Apple’s plans in streaming video, which one estimated could bring in $37 billion annually in a few years.
Don’t miss: Here’s what could happen to Apple’s average selling prices in the next iPhone cycle
“On net, we consider it plausible (albeit unlikely) that Apple will finally unveil its long-vaunted streaming service at next week’s iPhone announcement,” Bernstein’s Sacconaghi wrote. “If that is indeed the case, then a key question is what is Apple’s long-term goal for video streaming: would it be for ecosystem enhancement (e.g., Maps), revenue enhancement (Apple Music), or a combination of both (e.g. Apple Pay)?”
Apple shares are up 37% over the past 12 months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.44% of which Apple is a component, has gained 19%.
Emily Bary Emily Bary is a MarketWatch reporter based in New York.
